(1) SINGLE-RUNG LADDER. `VAULT_MIGRATIONS` holds one entry and a fresh vault stamps `PRAGMA user_version = 1`; `JOURNAL_MIGRATIONS` is gone. Every rung module (reconcile.ts, close-v0.ts, conventions*.ts, entity-*.ts shapes, share-grant.ts, the people cadence-floor and sync refresh-capability rungs) was deleted and its SHAPE folded into the band's DDL module, so the baseline states the target rather than reconstructing it. v0 has no files in the field; a rung that walks a vault nobody has is compatibility code for a problem nobody has.
(2) DROPPED TABLES, none of which can hold a row a bundle would lose: health.* (5), finance.* (5), core.observation + observation_component, home.* (5) and business.* (5) left the ontology (rulings ONT-06 / O-domains) and were never created; agent.correction, agent.judgment, access.app_view, access.export_job and schedule.availability_rule are machinery with no producer; social.contact_card folded onto people.profile + social.contact_channel (O-contact); tally.expense_receipt folded onto core.attachment role='receipt' (O-attach); share.grant and enrich.consent folded into share.authority (V-table); locker.item_history folded into core.entity_revision (D2). Each one's content is still in the canonical walk under the row that now owns it.

The consent plane became the ACCESS plane (D4): consent_* -> access_* physically and consent.* -> access.* logically, including the evidence stream (consent_provenance -> access_provenance, consent_receipt -> access_receipt) which is now one plane with one name. core_vault.owner_party_id -> self_party_id; core_share_origin.shared_by_member -> shared_by and item_* -> target_*; share_commons_lineage/retained item_* -> target_*; schedule_task.tz and tally_recurring_expense.tz (R4); schedule_recurrence_exception.original_start -> original_start_local (R5). Same cells, same values; exportVault's SELECT * carries them under the new names with no adapter.
(4) NEW TABLES, all registered or band-declared: core_entity + core_entity_kind (the supertype; LOCAL, because a restore re-derives every row through the membership triggers), schedule_recurrence_exception_attendee and tally_recurring_expense_split (party ids out of JSON and into rows, D3/R6), share_delivery_config, and the two bands below.
(5) THE ENTITY SUPERTYPE. Every ontology entity table gained `FOREIGN KEY (<pk>) REFERENCES core_entity(entity_id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, and all thirteen polymorphic `(type, id)` mechanisms became real composite foreign keys into `core_entity(entity_type, entity_id)`. The hand-kept poly-ref registry and its sweep are gone. Export completeness is unaffected: the supertype is derived, and every pointer's TARGET was already in the walk.
(6) THE AUDIT BAND, in the vault file. journal.db is deleted; access_provenance, agent_command_invocation, access_receipt, agent_invocation_check, agent_evidence, agent_explanation and audit_archive_manifest are bands of vault.db, append-only ENFORCED by BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers with one documented door (audit_archive_pass, held open only inside the archival transaction). A write and its receipt now share one transaction, and core_entity_revision.invocation_id is a REAL key (ON DELETE SET NULL).
(7) THE LEDGER BAND, in the vault file: the conversation transcript (conversations/turns/items/attachments and their archival tables) moved from journal.db into packages/vault/src/schema/ledger.ts. The vault package owns the tables; the server engine owns the store code and receives the vault connection.
EXPORT COMPLETENESS RE-AUDITED in packages/vault/src/gateway/portable-export.ts. The `audit` and `ledger` bands are excluded from the portable export and from the replica BY BAND — named from their band modules (AUDIT_BAND_TABLES / LEDGER_BAND_TABLES) into LOCAL_TABLES, so adding a table to either cannot silently add it to a bundle — and their size is bounded by RETENTION_WINDOWS in schema/audit.ts rather than by living in a second file. A backup still carries the whole file, encrypted, by design: a backup that dropped the evidence would restore a vault that could not prove its own history. Every other table stays in the canonical walk, exportVault's SELECT * carries every added column (updated_at/created_at on the tables that gained one, currency on the Tally ledger, seq on access_receipt, invocation_id on core_entity_revision) with no adapter, and no sealed cell changed class.

Two DDL modules moved and NO table, column or CHECK value changed with them, so the canonical walk is byte-identical and `exportVault`'s `SELECT *` carries exactly what it carried before. `schema/entity.ts`: the generated membership trigger gained a `RAISE(ABORT)` guard ahead of its unchanged `INSERT OR IGNORE`, refusing an `entity_id` another kind already holds — `OR IGNORE` stays because SQLite fires BEFORE INSERT triggers ahead of conflict resolution, so every upsert and every restore re-derives a supertype row that is already there; and `core_entity_revoke_on_purge`'s principal clause is generated from `PRINCIPAL_ENTITY_KINDS` instead of hard-coding `'person'`, so purging a circle revokes the answers held through it. `schema/authority.ts` adds that map and its non-entity counterpart. `core_entity` is LOCAL either way — a restore re-derives every row through these same triggers — so a guard that refuses a cross-kind collision cannot remove anything a bundle carried.
